sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: The dynasty was founded by **Pilaji Rao Gaekwad**, a lieutenant of the Senapati Khanderao Dabhade, who established his base in Gujarat.
• **Territorial Base**: The Gaekwads consolidated power in **Baroda (Vadodara)**, which became the capital of their princely state.
• **Confederacy Status**: As a key member of the **Maratha Confederacy**, they held the right to collect *Chauth* and *Sardeshmukhi* in the Gujarat region.
• **Key Metric**: The transition from military commanders under the Peshwa to autonomous rulers under the British **Subsidiary Alliance (1802)**.

items.definition: An agreement signed by Anand Rao Gaekwad with the British, effectively ending Gaekwad independence and placing the state under British protection.
The most reformist ruler (1875-1939) known for social reforms, education (compulsory primary education), and industrialization.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Social Reform**: Sayaji Rao III introduced the **Compulsory Education Act (1906)**, a pioneer in India.
• **Economic Policy**: Establishment of the **Bank of Baroda (1908)** to foster local trade and industry.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Challenges**: Constant friction with the Peshwa for revenue control; later, British interference in succession disputes.
• **Solutions**: Modernization of administration and focus on public welfare to maintain legitimacy.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'P-D-S' (Pilaji, Dabhade, Subsidiary).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Pilaji founded it, Dabhade was the original patron, Subsidiary Alliance defined their colonial end-state.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Gaekwads with the Holkars or Scindias. Remember: Gaekwad = Baroda, Holkar = Indore, Scindia = Gwalior.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Progressive Princely State' when discussing Sayaji Rao III's contributions to social legislation.

keyTakeaways: The Gaekwads were instrumental in the Maratha expansion into Gujarat.
The 1802 Subsidiary Alliance marked the shift from Maratha vassal to British protectorate.
Sayaji Rao III is a critical figure for questions on social reform and administrative modernization in Princely States.
